newsitem.title: USA: Iraqi defenses heavily damaged - Pentagon.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi defenses heavily damaged - Pentagon.

text.p: U.S. cruise missiles scored a "severe degradation" of Iraqi anti-aircraft defences, destroying or damaging as many as 11 of 15 targets, the Pentagon said on Friday in its first detailed assessment of raids on southern Iraq.

"The overall assessment was that the two strikes...achieved a severe degradation of Iraq defences south of the 33rd parallel," Defence Department spokesman Ken Bacon said of the 44 missiles fired from warships and bombers on Monday and Tuesday.

Stressing that the damage assessment was not complete, Bacon said the Tomahawk ship-launched missiles and other cruise missiles fired by B-52 bombers were aimed at eight surface-to-air (SAM) missile sites and seven air defence command and control facilities.

Bacon said five of the eight SAM sites were "severely damaged or destroyed" and at least one other damaged or vacated. One command site was destroyed or severely damaged and four others were damaged, vacated or degraded, he added.

He said the final results of the strikes had not been determined by U.S. intelligence but that the satellite-guided missiles, designed to land within a 12-meter radius circle from more than 500 miles (800 km) away at least half of the time, had performed well generally.

"We are not flawless and the weapons do not meet their specifications 100 per cent of the time," said Bacon, adding that two anti-aircraft missile launchers had been moved before the attack and two command sites received only minor or no damage at all.
